headline_marked: Mbappe brace as [[France beat Iraq 3-0]] to reach knockouts
headline: Mbappe brace as France beat Iraq 3-0 to reach knockouts
summary: Kylian Mbappe scores his second brace of the tournament, equaling Miroslav Klose's all-time World Cup goal record with 16 goals.
details: France secured a 3-0 victory over Iraq on Monday, ensuring their progression to the round of 32. Kylian Mbappe led the charge with two goals, while Ousmane Dembele added a third.
Mbappe's brace brought his total to 16 all-time World Cup goals, pulling him level with former record-holder Miroslav Klose. He now trails Lionel Messi's new benchmark of 18 career World Cup goals.
The match was significantly disrupted by severe thunderstorms, which caused a lengthy weather stoppage. The second-half kickoff was delayed by nearly two hours, forcing spectators to seek shelter.
France dominated the early stages of the game, with Mbappe scoring in the 14th minute. He later capitalized on a goal-kick error by Iraq to score his second.

Iraq remains in contention for one of the eight knockout spots reserved for third-place teams. However, they face a difficult path, likely needing a win against Senegal and favorable results elsewhere.
France's final group match will be against Norway, while Iraq may be without key player Aymen Hussein, who exited the match in the 26th minute with an injury.
caption:
Kylian Mbappe hits 16 World Cup goals to equal Miroslav Klose's record as France cruises into the knockouts!

France secured a 3-0 victory over Iraq on Monday, ensuring their progression to the round of 32. Kylian Mbappe led the charge with two goals, while Ousmane Dembele added a third.

Mbappe's brace brought his total to 16 all-time World Cup goals, pulling him level with former record-holder Miroslav Klose. He now trails Lionel Messi's new benchmark of 18 career World Cup goals.

The match was significantly disrupted by severe thunderstorms, which caused a lengthy weather stoppage. The second-half kickoff was delayed by nearly two hours, forcing spectators to seek shelter.

France dominated the early stages of the game, with Mbappe scoring in the 14th minute. He later capitalized on a goal-kick error by Iraq to score his second.

Iraq remains in contention for one of the eight knockout spots reserved for third-place teams. However, they face a difficult path, likely needing a win against Senegal and favorable results elsewhere.

France's final group match will be against Norway, while Iraq may be without key player Aymen Hussein, who exited the match in the 26th minute with an injury.

headline_marked: Govt plan: [[MPs to get 50 crore BDT each]] for local infrastructure
headline: Govt plan: MPs to get 50 crore BDT each for local infrastructure
summary: The proposed project will allocate 10 crore BDT annually over five years for 279 MPs to develop roads and rural infrastructure in their constituencies.
details: The government is proposing a project to allocate 50 crore BDT to each of the 279 Members of Parliament (MPs) for the development of roads and rural infrastructure in their respective constituencies.

Under this plan, MPs will receive 10 crore BDT annually over five years. The Local Government Engineering Department (LGED) has sent the proposal to the Ministry of Local Government, with a total estimated cost of approximately 15,000 crore BDT.
MPs will provide a list of priority projects, such as roads, bridges, culverts, and markets, which the LGED will then implement. This system of MP allocations began in the 2005-06 fiscal year.
To improve management and oversight, the current government plans to implement the project through eight separate projects—one for each administrative division—rather than a single national project.

The allocation will not apply to 21 seats within city corporations or the 50 reserved seats for women MPs. The total cost for the 279 eligible MPs is estimated at 13,950 crore BDT, plus 1,000 crore BDT for administrative costs.
LGED officials stated that the allocation has increased due to rising construction material costs and inflation, which are expected to continue over the next five years.
While some MPs argue these funds are essential for urgent local development, critics have previously raised concerns regarding nepotism, corruption, and the quality of work in such projects.
